children: , the data-center and personal-computing chipmaker, carried Monday's Muse-driven CPU enthusiasm into Tuesday, with shares gaining approximately 0.5% to $122.46. The valuation picture is much louder than the daily move: Intel now trades 281.26% above its $32.12 GF Value estimate, signaling that investors are pricing in a far more aggressive recovery and AI opportunity than the historical valuation framework suggests.

Meta's Muse agent shows why CPUs could still matter in an AI market dominated by accelerator headlines. The agent operates through its own virtual computer and can keep working on longer tasks even after a user exits the application, creating demand for general-purpose compute around the model itself. Intel is trying to capture that layer as its business rebounds, with second-quarter revenue rising 25% to $16.1 billion and the company rolling out its Xeon 6+ server processor built on Intel 18A.

But Muse is evidence of a potentially expanding workload, not evidence of an Intel design win. That distinction matters at a stock price already sitting dramatically above GF Value. The real payoff comes only if autonomous agents drive incremental server deployments and Intel wins enough of that spending at attractive margins. Xeon availability, power efficiency, hyperscaler adoption and Intel 18A execution are therefore the numbers investors should watch before assuming the AI-agent boom automatically turns into Intel profits.

title: Intel Drops as Muse Revives the Server CPU Thesis
